questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I have __the bestest__ placement offer among all my classmates.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **the best**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The error lies in the use of the non-standard word "**bestest**." 
 
• In formal or standard English, "**best**" is already the superlative form of "**good**," and adding "-**est**" to it creates redundancy.
 
• "**the best**" is grammatically correct and conveys the intended meaning effectively.
 
• It indicates that the speaker's placement offer is superior to those of their classmates.
 
• "**Best**" is the superlative form of the adjective "**good**," indicating the **highest level of quality**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**.

**Corrected sentence**: *I have the best__ placement offer among all my classmates.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• "**Better**" is the comparative form of good, it doesn't fit well in this context.
 
• "**More**" is used to form the comparative degree of adjectives with more than one syllable (e.g., more beautiful, more intelligent).
 
• "**Good**" is a positive adjective, it doesn't convey the idea of superiority or excellence as effectively as "**the best**" does.

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. Some residents saw this as an opportunity for growth and prosperity, while others feared that it would destroy the town's unique character.

B. The small town of Millfield was known for its charming Main Street, where locals and visitors alike could stroll among the quaint shops and cafes.

C. The debate grew heated, and tensions rose as the town struggled to decide its future.

D. One day, a large corporation announced its plans to build a massive shopping centre on the outskirts of town.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **BDAC**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Part B**. The paragraph begins by introducing the small town of Millfield and its charming Main Street, setting the scene and providing context for the events that follow.
 
• **Part D**. The sentence follows logically after the introduction of Millfield in sentence B. It introduces the conflict or catalyst of the story: the announcement of a large corporation's plans to build a massive shopping centre on the outskirts of town.
 
• **Part A**. After the announcement of the corporation's plans, the paragraph addresses the reaction of the town's residents.
 
• **Part C**. Finally, the paragraph concludes with the escalation of the conflict as tensions rise among the townspeople. 

Therefore, the sequence **BDAC **creates a coherent and meaningful paragraph by establishing the setting, introducing the conflict, exploring the reactions of the townspeople, and concluding with the escalation of tension and debate.

Hence, the correct answer is **option 1**.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

The company will release the new product next month.

options.text: The new product will be released by the company next month.
The new product will release by the company next month.
The new product will be releasing by the company next month.
The new product is released by the company next month.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **The new product will be released by the company next month**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **subject** of the Active Voice is changed into the **object** of the Passive voice. Also, the **object **of the Active Voice is changed into the **subject** of the Passive Voice.
 
• The usage of a **helping verb** is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.
 
• The preposition **“by”** is used before the object made in Passive Voice. However, it is optional in some cases.
 
• The Active voice in this question is in **Future Indefinite**. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in the **Future Indefinite**.
 
• The format of Active voice is: **Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object**.
 
• Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: **Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + made + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).**
 
• For example:
 
 
• He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)
 
• The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• The options except (1) don’t follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: ***The new product will be released by the company next month.***
